title: Spaghetti Aglio e Olio
description: Garlic, oil, chile and pasta water. Four ingredients, fifteen minutes.
steps: Boil the pasta in well-salted water until just shy of al dente, 1 minute less than the package says. Reserve 2 cups of the cooking water before draining - this starchy water is the sauce.
While it cooks, warm the olive oil with the sliced garlic in a wide skillet over medium-low. Cook 4-5 minutes until the garlic is pale gold and no further. Browned garlic turns the whole dish bitter.
Add the red pepper flakes for 30 seconds.
Add the drained pasta to the skillet with 1 cup of the pasta water and toss hard over medium heat for 2 minutes. The starch and oil will emulsify into a glossy sauce that clings.
Add more pasta water if it looks dry. Off the heat, toss in the parsley, Parmesan and black pepper.

title: Spaghetti Carbonara
description: Eggs, pecorino, guanciale and pepper. No cream, ever.
steps: Whisk the egg yolks, whole eggs, Pecorino and black pepper into a thick paste and set it aside. This is the entire sauce.
Render the diced guanciale in a cold skillet over medium heat until the fat has melted out and the meat is crisp, 8 minutes. Leave the fat in the pan and take it off the heat.
Boil the spaghetti in salted water to al dente, reserving 2 cups of the water.
Add the drained hot pasta to the skillet of warm fat off the heat and toss to coat.

Now, with the pan still off the heat, pour in the egg mixture and toss fast and constantly, adding splashes of pasta water until it turns creamy. Any direct heat at this stage scrambles the eggs - the pasta's residual heat is all you need.
Serve immediately with more Pecorino and pepper. Carbonara does not wait.

title: Cacio e Pepe
description: Pecorino and black pepper emulsified into a sauce with pasta water alone.
ingredients: 1 tbsp whole black peppercorns, coarsely ground
steps: Grate the Pecorino as finely as you can - coarse shreds will not melt smoothly and are the usual cause of a clumpy sauce.
Toast the coarsely ground pepper in a dry skillet 30 seconds until fragrant.
Boil the pasta in less water than usual and only lightly salted, since Pecorino is very salty. The water will be extra starchy, which you want. Reserve 2 cups.
Mix the Pecorino with about 1/2 cup of the hot pasta water in a bowl to make a smooth, thick paste. Let it cool for a moment - cheese added to boiling liquid seizes into strings.
Add the drained pasta to the skillet with the pepper and a splash of water, then take it off the heat and stir in the cheese paste, tossing vigorously.
Add water a tablespoon at a time until it is creamy and coats each strand. Serve at once.

title: Spaghetti Marinara
description: A 30-minute tomato sauce from canned tomatoes, garlic and basil.
ingredients: 1 can (28 oz) San Marzano tomatoes, crushed by hand
steps: Warm the olive oil with the garlic over medium-low 3-4 minutes until fragrant and barely colored.
Add the pepper flakes, then the tomatoes, crushing each one in your hand as it goes in. Hand-crushed tomatoes give a better texture than blended.
Add the salt and sugar - the sugar is there to balance the acid of canned tomatoes, not to sweeten - and simmer 25-30 minutes until the sauce darkens and the oil separates slightly at the edges.
Tear in most of the basil in the last 2 minutes.
Boil the pasta to al dente, reserving a cup of water. Toss the pasta in the sauce with a splash of that water for 1 minute so it absorbs.
Serve with Parmesan and the remaining basil.

title: Spaghetti and Meatballs
description: Tender meatballs simmered in tomato sauce - the Italian-American classic.
steps: Soak the breadcrumbs in the milk for 5 minutes. This panade is the single reason good meatballs are tender rather than dense.
Mix in both meats, the eggs, half the Parmesan, half the garlic, the parsley, salt and pepper with your hands, stopping as soon as it comes together.
Roll into 18 balls and brown them in the olive oil in batches, 2 minutes per side. They do not need to cook through.
Cook the onion in the same pot 6 minutes, add the rest of the garlic, then the tomatoes and oregano.
Return the meatballs, cover and simmer very gently 40 minutes. Do not stir hard or they break up.
Tear in the basil, boil the spaghetti to al dente, and serve with the sauce and remaining Parmesan.

title: Tagliatelle Bolognese
description: A proper ragu: milk, wine and three hours of the lowest possible simmer.
steps: Cook the onion, carrot and celery in the oil and butter over medium-low for 12 minutes until completely soft and sweet. Rushing this soffritto costs you the base of the whole sauce.
Add both meats and cook, breaking them up, until no pink remains but without letting them brown hard, 10 minutes.
Pour in the milk and simmer until it has almost entirely evaporated, about 15 minutes. The milk tenderizes the meat and is not optional in a real bolognese.
Add the wine and reduce the same way, 15 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste, then the crushed tomatoes, salt, pepper and nutmeg. Bring to the barest simmer - a bubble every few seconds.
Cook uncovered 2.5-3 hours, stirring occasionally, until deep brick-red and thick. Toss with cooked tagliatelle and a ladle of pasta water, and finish with Parmesan.

title: Classic Lasagna
description: Layers of meat sauce, bechamel and pasta baked until the top is blistered.
steps: Brown both meats in the oil, add the onion for 6 minutes and the garlic for 1, then the tomato paste for 2 minutes. Add the tomatoes, oregano, salt and pepper and simmer 45 minutes until thick.
Make the bechamel: melt the butter, whisk in the flour and cook 2 minutes, then add the warm milk gradually, whisking, and simmer 5 minutes until it coats a spoon. Season with nutmeg and salt.
Boil the noodles 2 minutes less than the package says, then lay them flat on oiled sheets so they do not stick together.
Build in a 9x13 dish: meat sauce, noodles, bechamel, mozzarella, Parmesan. Repeat four times, finishing with bechamel and a heavy layer of both cheeses.
Bake at 375F for 45-50 minutes until deeply browned and bubbling at the edges. Cover with foil if the top colors too fast.
Rest at least 30 minutes before cutting. This is the step everyone skips, and it is the difference between neat squares and a landslide.

title: Baked Ziti
description: Ricotta, sauce and mozzarella baked over pasta. Lasagna without the layering.
steps: Brown the sausage in the oil, breaking it up, then add the onion for 6 minutes and the garlic for 1.
Add the tomatoes, oregano, pepper flakes and salt and simmer 20 minutes.
Boil the pasta 3 minutes short of al dente. It will finish in the oven, and fully cooked pasta turns to mush in a bake.
Stir the ricotta with the egg, half the Parmesan and a pinch of salt.
Toss the drained pasta with most of the sauce, then layer half into a 9x13 dish, dollop the ricotta over, add the rest of the pasta, the remaining sauce, mozzarella and Parmesan.
Bake at 400F for 25 minutes until bubbling and browned. Rest 10 minutes and top with torn basil.

title: Penne alla Vodka
description: Tomato, cream and vodka cooked into a silky pink sauce.
steps: Cook the shallot in the oil over medium 4 minutes, then the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the tomato paste and pepper flakes and fry 4-5 minutes, stirring, until the paste darkens from bright red to brick. This frying step is what gives the sauce its depth.
Pour in the vodka and let it bubble down by half, 2-3 minutes. The alcohol cooks off and leaves a sharpness that cuts the cream.
Lower the heat and stir in the cream and salt. Simmer 5 minutes.
Boil the penne to al dente, reserving a cup of water, then toss it in the sauce with a splash of that water for 2 minutes.
Finish off the heat with the Parmesan and torn basil.

title: Fettuccine Alfredo
description: Butter, Parmesan and pasta water tossed into a glossy coating.
steps: Grate the Parmesan very finely. Coarse cheese is the main reason home Alfredo turns stringy.
Boil the fettuccine in salted water to al dente, reserving 2 cups of water.
Melt the butter in a wide skillet with 1 cup of the pasta water, swirling until it emulsifies into a cloudy sauce.
Add the drained pasta and toss over low heat 1 minute.
Take the pan off the heat and add the Parmesan in three handfuls, tossing constantly and adding pasta water as needed. Off the heat is essential - boiling makes the cheese clump.
Season with pepper and nutmeg and serve immediately. Real Alfredo has no cream and no flour.

title: Pasta Primavera
description: Spring vegetables tossed with pasta, lemon and Parmesan.
steps: Boil the pasta to al dente in salted water, reserving a cup of water.

Cook the onion and carrots in the oil over high heat 4 minutes, then add the zucchini, squash and bell pepper for 4 minutes. Keep the heat high and the pan uncrowded so the vegetables brown instead of steaming.
Add the asparagus, peas and garlic and cook 2 minutes. The vegetables should stay crisp.
Stir in the cream, lemon juice, zest, salt and pepper and simmer 2 minutes.
Add the pasta and a splash of its water and toss for 1 minute.
Finish off the heat with the Parmesan and basil.

title: Linguine with Basil Pesto
description: Raw basil, pine nut and Parmesan sauce, never cooked.
steps: Toast the pine nuts in a dry pan 3 minutes until golden, shaking often, then cool completely.
Pulse the basil, pine nuts and garlic in a food processor until coarsely chopped. Pulse rather than run it - blending heats the basil and turns it black.
Add the Parmesan, then drizzle in the olive oil with the motor running until it forms a loose paste. Season with salt, pepper and lemon juice.
Boil the pasta to al dente and reserve a cup of water.
Toss the drained pasta with the pesto off the heat, loosening with pasta water. Never cook pesto in a hot pan - heat dulls it and turns it bitter.
Serve with extra Parmesan.

title: Bucatini all'Amatriciana
description: Guanciale, tomato and Pecorino - a Roman classic with three ingredients.
ingredients: 1 can (28 oz) San Marzano tomatoes, crushed by hand
steps: Render the guanciale in a cold dry skillet over medium heat 8-10 minutes until the fat has melted out and the strips are crisp at the edges.
Lift out half the guanciale to keep crisp for serving, leaving all the fat behind.
Add the pepper flakes for 30 seconds, then the hand-crushed tomatoes and salt.
Simmer 20 minutes until the sauce thickens and takes on a glossy orange color from the pork fat.
Boil the bucatini to al dente and toss it in the sauce with a splash of pasta water for 1 minute.
Take it off the heat and toss in most of the Pecorino, then serve topped with the reserved guanciale, more cheese and black pepper.

title: Spaghetti alla Puttanesca
description: Anchovy, olive, caper and tomato sauce built entirely from the pantry.
ingredients: 1 cup Kalamata olives, pitted and halved
steps: Warm the oil with the anchovies over medium-low, mashing them with a spoon until they dissolve completely, 2-3 minutes. They will not taste fishy - they taste savory.
Add the garlic and pepper flakes for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, olives, capers and oregano and simmer 18-20 minutes.
Taste before adding any salt. Anchovies, olives and capers are all salty, and this sauce often needs none.
Boil the spaghetti to al dente and toss it in the sauce with a splash of pasta water.
Finish with parsley.

title: Penne all'Arrabbiata
description: An angry sauce: garlic, chile and tomato, nothing else.
steps: Warm the oil with the garlic over medium-low until it just turns pale gold, 3 minutes.
Add a generous amount of pepper flakes and fry 30 seconds. The heat is meant to be assertive - arrabbiata means angry.
Add the tomatoes and salt and simmer 20 minutes until thickened and the oil separates at the edges.
Boil the penne to al dente, reserving a cup of water.
Toss the pasta in the sauce with a splash of water for 1 minute, then add the parsley.
Serve with Pecorino, which cuts the heat.

title: Shrimp Scampi
description: Garlic, butter, white wine and lemon with shrimp over linguine.
steps: Boil the linguine to al dente, reserving a cup of water.
Pat the shrimp dry, season, and sear in the olive oil over high heat 1 minute per side. Pull them out while barely pink - they finish in the sauce.
Lower the heat, add 2 tbsp butter and the garlic and pepper flakes and cook 1 minute without browning the garlic.
Pour in the wine and reduce by half, 3 minutes, scraping the pan.
Whisk in the remaining butter a cube at a time off the heat so the sauce emulsifies rather than splits, then add the lemon juice and zest.
Return the shrimp and the pasta with a splash of water, toss 1 minute, and finish with parsley and Parmesan.

title: Linguine alle Vongole
description: Clams steamed open in white wine and garlic, their liquor becoming the sauce.
steps: Scrub the clams and soak them in cold salted water 20 minutes to purge sand, then lift them out rather than pouring, leaving the grit behind.
Start the pasta in salted water, aiming to drain it 2 minutes underdone.
Warm the oil with the garlic and pepper flakes over medium 2 minutes, then add the wine and bring to a boil.
Add the clams, cover, and steam 5-7 minutes until they open. Discard any that stay shut.
Lift the clams out, leaving the liquid. Add the underdone pasta directly to that liquid and cook 2 minutes, tossing, so it drinks the clam broth - this is where the flavor goes.
Return the clams, swirl in the butter off the heat, and finish with parsley and pepper. Do not add cheese.

title: Pasta e Fagioli
description: Beans and small pasta in a thick, soupy stew. Peasant food at its best.
ingredients: 2 cans (15 oz each) cannellini beans, drained
steps: Render the pancetta in the oil 5 minutes, then add the onion, carrots and celery and cook 8 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic, tomato paste and pepper flakes and cook 2 minutes.

Mash about a third of the beans with a fork, then add all the beans, the broth, the Parmesan rind and the rosemary. The mashed beans thicken the soup naturally and the rind adds savoriness as it softens.
Simmer 20 minutes, then add the pasta and cook until al dente, 8-9 minutes.
Fish out the Parmesan rind and season. The soup should be thick enough that a spoon stands up briefly - add broth if it is too tight.
Serve with Parmesan, parsley and a drizzle of olive oil.

title: Orecchiette with Sausage and Broccoli Rabe
description: Bitter greens, fennel-scented sausage and ear-shaped pasta.
steps: Blanch the broccoli rabe in the boiling salted pasta water for 2 minutes, then lift it out and squeeze dry. Blanching tames the bitterness - skipping it leaves the dish harsh.
Cook the pasta in that same water to al dente, reserving 2 cups.
Brown the sausage in the oil over medium-high, breaking it into chunks rather than crumbs, 8 minutes.
Add the garlic and pepper flakes for 1 minute, then the chopped broccoli rabe for 3 minutes.
Add the pasta and a cup of the water and toss hard for 2 minutes until a light sauce forms.
Finish off the heat with Pecorino and black pepper.

title: Pasta alla Norma
description: Fried eggplant in tomato sauce with salty ricotta salata. Sicily's classic.
steps: Toss the eggplant cubes with the salt and leave them in a colander 30 minutes, then rinse and press dry. This draws out bitterness and, more importantly, stops them absorbing the whole bottle of oil.
Fry the eggplant in batches in most of the olive oil over medium-high until deep golden on all sides, 8 minutes per batch. Drain on paper towels.
In the same pan, cook the garlic and pepper flakes in the remaining oil 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and salt and simmer 15 minutes, then return three quarters of the eggplant.
Boil the rigatoni to al dente and toss it in the sauce with a splash of pasta water.
Serve topped with the reserved eggplant, torn basil and a heavy snowfall of ricotta salata.

title: Stuffed Shells
description: Jumbo shells piped full of ricotta and spinach, baked under marinara.
ingredients: 10 oz frozen spinach, thawed and squeezed dry
steps: Boil the shells 2 minutes less than the package says, then spread them on a sheet pan to cool. Undercooking matters - they finish in the oven and tear if fully cooked.
Squeeze every drop of water from the spinach. Wet spinach makes a loose, watery filling.
Mix the ricotta, spinach, eggs, 1 cup mozzarella, 1 cup Parmesan, nutmeg, salt and pepper.
Spread 2 cups of marinara in a 9x13 dish. Fill each shell with a heaped spoonful or a piping bag and set them in the dish open side up.
Spoon the remaining sauce over, then the rest of the mozzarella and Parmesan.
Cover with foil and bake at 375F for 30 minutes, then uncover for 15 minutes until bubbling and browned. Rest 10 minutes and add basil.

title: Manicotti
description: Crepe-wrapped ricotta baked in tomato sauce - more tender than pasta tubes.
steps: Whisk the flour, milk, 4 eggs and 1/2 tsp salt into a thin batter and let it rest 20 minutes. Resting lets the flour hydrate so the crepes do not tear.
Cook 16 thin crepes in a buttered 7-inch nonstick pan, about 45 seconds per side, stacking them as you go.
Mix the ricotta, 1 cup mozzarella, 1 cup Parmesan, the remaining egg, parsley, nutmeg, salt and pepper.
Spread 2 cups marinara in a 9x13 dish. Put a line of filling along one edge of each crepe and roll it up, then set them seam-side down in the dish.
Cover with the remaining sauce and the rest of the cheeses.
Bake at 375F for 40-45 minutes until bubbling and browned at the edges. Rest 10 minutes before serving.

title: Ravioli with Brown Butter and Sage
description: Store-bought ravioli elevated by browned butter and crisp sage.
steps: Boil the ravioli in salted water according to the package, usually 4-5 minutes. Keep the water at a gentle simmer so they do not burst.
Meanwhile melt the butter in a light-colored skillet over medium heat. A light pan lets you see the color change.
Cook the butter 4-6 minutes, swirling, until the milk solids turn golden brown and it smells nutty. Watch it constantly - the gap between brown butter and burnt butter is about 30 seconds.
Add the sage leaves and walnuts and cook 1 minute until the sage crisps.
Lift the ravioli straight from the water into the pan with a little of the cooking water and toss gently.
Season, add the lemon juice to cut the richness, and serve with Parmesan.

title: Gnocchi al Pomodoro
description: Pillowy potato dumplings in simple tomato sauce with torn mozzarella.
steps: Warm the oil with the garlic and pepper flakes 2 minutes, then add the tomatoes and salt and simmer 18 minutes.
Boil the gnocchi in salted water. They are done the moment they float to the surface, usually 2-3 minutes. Leaving them in longer makes them gluey.
Lift them out with a slotted spoon straight into the sauce along with a splash of the cooking water.
Toss gently for 1 minute - gnocchi are delicate and break if stirred roughly.
Take off the heat, scatter the torn mozzarella over and cover 2 minutes so it softens without fully melting away.
Finish with basil and Parmesan.

title: Tortellini in Brodo
description: Cheese tortellini floated in a clear, well-seasoned broth. Christmas in Emilia.
steps: Simmer the broth with the Parmesan rind and bay leaf for 20 minutes, then remove both. The rind turns an ordinary broth into something worth serving on its own.
Taste the broth and season it properly - in this dish it is the main event, not a background.
Bring it to a gentle simmer and add the tortellini. Cook them in the broth itself, 3-4 minutes, so the starch lightly thickens it.
Add the nutmeg and pepper.
Ladle into warm bowls, making sure everyone gets plenty of broth, and serve with Parmesan and parsley.

title: Pasta al Limone
description: Cream, lemon and Parmesan in a bright sauce that takes ten minutes.
steps: Boil the pasta in salted water to al dente and reserve 2 cups of water.
Melt the butter in a wide skillet, add the cream and the lemon zest and simmer 3 minutes.
Take the pan off the heat before adding the lemon juice. Acid added to simmering cream can curdle it.
Add the drained pasta and a cup of pasta water and toss over low heat 1 minute.
Off the heat, add the Parmesan in handfuls, tossing until the sauce turns silky. Loosen with more pasta water if needed.
Season generously and finish with basil.

title: Pasta with Sausage and Peppers
description: Sweet Italian sausage and charred peppers in a light tomato sauce.
steps: Brown the sausage in the oil over medium-high, breaking it into large chunks, 8 minutes. Leave the chunks big - they stay juicier than crumbles.
Add the peppers and onion and cook 8 minutes over high heat until charred at the edges.
Add the garlic and pepper flakes for 1 minute, then the tomatoes, salt and oregano.
Simmer 12 minutes while the pasta boils to al dente.
Toss the pasta into the sauce with a splash of pasta water for 2 minutes.
Finish with Parmesan and basil.

title: Chicken Alfredo
description: Seared chicken over fettuccine in a cream and Parmesan sauce.
steps: Pound the chicken to an even thickness, season with salt, pepper and garlic powder, and sear in the olive oil 5-6 minutes per side until 165F inside. Rest it on a board.
Boil the fettuccine to al dente, reserving 2 cups of water.
Melt the butter in the same skillet, add the garlic for 1 minute without browning it.
Pour in the cream and simmer 4 minutes until slightly thickened.
Take the pan off the heat and add the Parmesan in handfuls, whisking. Off-heat is what keeps the sauce smooth rather than grainy. Loosen with pasta water.
Toss the pasta in the sauce, slice the rested chicken and lay it over the top with parsley and nutmeg.

title: Pasta alla Gricia
description: Carbonara without the eggs: guanciale, Pecorino, pepper and pasta water.
steps: Render the guanciale in a cold dry skillet over medium heat 10 minutes until crisp. Lift out half for serving and keep all the fat.
Toast the black pepper in the fat for 30 seconds.
Boil the pasta in lightly salted water - Pecorino is salty - and reserve 2 cups of water.
Add a cup of pasta water to the skillet and bring to a simmer so it emulsifies with the fat into a cloudy sauce.
Add the drained pasta and toss 1 minute, then take the pan off the heat and add the Pecorino in handfuls, tossing hard. Direct heat at this point makes it clump.
Serve with the reserved guanciale and more pepper.

title: Gnocchi alla Sorrentina
description: Gnocchi baked in tomato sauce under mozzarella until browned and bubbling.
steps: Warm the oil with the garlic and pepper flakes 2 minutes, add the tomatoes and salt and simmer 20 minutes until thick.
Boil the gnocchi only until they float, 2 minutes, then lift them out. They will finish in the oven, so err on the side of underdone.
Fold the gnocchi into the sauce with half the basil and pour into a baking dish.
Scatter the torn mozzarella and Parmesan over the top.
Bake at 425F for 15 minutes until the cheese is melted and browned in patches.
Rest 5 minutes and finish with the remaining basil.

title: Italian Pasta Salad
description: Rotini, salami, mozzarella and vegetables in red wine vinaigrette.
steps: Cook the pasta to just past al dente - pasta firms up when cold, so slightly soft now is right - then rinse under cold water and drain well.
Shake or whisk the vinegar, oil, Dijon, garlic, oregano, salt and pepper into a vinaigrette.
Toss the warm pasta with half the dressing. Warm pasta absorbs it; cold pasta just gets coated.
Add the salami, mozzarella, tomatoes, cucumber, olives and red onion.
Chill at least 1 hour, then add the remaining dressing, Parmesan and basil just before serving. Pasta salad always needs more dressing and salt after chilling than you expect.

title: Fresh Egg Pasta Dough
description: Flour and eggs kneaded, rested and rolled thin. The foundation of everything.
ingredients: 3 1/2 cups all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
steps: Mound the flour on a board, make a deep well in the center and add the eggs, yolks, oil and salt. Break the eggs up with a fork and gradually pull flour in from the walls of the well.

Once it holds together, knead for a full 10 minutes. The dough should go from shaggy to smooth and springy - when you press it, the dent should slowly fill back in. Underkneaded dough tears when rolled.
Wrap tightly and rest at room temperature at least 30 minutes. This relaxes the gluten; skip it and the dough fights you.
Cut off a quarter of the dough, keeping the rest wrapped, and flatten it. Roll it through a pasta machine from the widest setting down, two passes per setting, until you can see your hand through it.
Dust with semolina - not flour, which absorbs and turns gummy - and cut into tagliatelle or sheets for lasagna and ravioli.
Cook fresh pasta in heavily salted boiling water for 90 seconds to 3 minutes. It is done almost as soon as it floats.

title: Sunday Gravy
description: Italian-American tomato sauce simmered all day with four kinds of meat.
steps: Brown the ribs, sausages and beef in the oil in batches in a large heavy pot, taking your time to get real color on each. This browning is the backbone of the sauce.
Cook the onions in the same pot 8 minutes, then the garlic for 1, then the tomato paste for 3 minutes until it darkens.
Add the wine, scrape the bottom clean, and reduce by half.
Add the tomatoes, herbs, salt, pepper and Parmesan rind, then return all the browned meat. Bring to the barest simmer.
Cook partially covered 3-4 hours, stirring every half hour and skimming fat from the surface. Add the meatballs in the last hour so they do not disintegrate.
Pull the meats out onto a platter to serve as a second course, and toss the sauce with the rigatoni and Parmesan.

title: Linguine ai Frutti di Mare
description: Shrimp, clams, mussels and calamari in a light tomato and wine broth.
steps: Scrub the shellfish and discard any that are cracked or stay open when tapped.
Warm the oil with the garlic and pepper flakes 2 minutes, add the wine and boil 2 minutes, then the tomatoes and salt. Simmer 15 minutes.
Add the clams first, cover and cook 4 minutes, then the mussels for 3 minutes until they open. The staggered timing matters - clams take longer than mussels.
Add the shrimp and calamari and cook 2 minutes only. Calamari turns to rubber after about 3 minutes of simmering.
Boil the linguine to just under al dente and add it to the pan with a splash of pasta water, tossing 1 minute.
Swirl in the butter off the heat, add the parsley, and discard any shells that did not open. No cheese with seafood pasta.

title: Pasta e Ceci
description: Chickpeas and pasta in a rosemary-scented stew. Pantry dinner in 30 minutes.
steps: Warm the oil with the garlic and pepper flakes 2 minutes, then add the tomato paste and fry 3 minutes until it darkens.
Blend or mash half the chickpeas with a cup of the broth and add it to the pot along with the whole chickpeas. The puree is what gives this its creamy body without any dairy.
Add the rest of the broth and the rosemary and simmer 10 minutes.
Add the pasta and cook until al dente, 8-9 minutes, stirring often since it thickens and can catch.
Pull out the rosemary stems, season, and let it sit 5 minutes - it should be thick, not soupy.
Serve with Parmesan, parsley and a heavy drizzle of olive oil.

title: Neapolitan Pizza Margherita
description: Slow-fermented dough, San Marzano, fior di latte, basil. The original.
ingredients: 12 oz fior di latte or fresh mozzarella, torn and drained
steps: Dissolve the yeast in the cold water, then mix in the flour and salt until no dry flour remains. Knead 10 minutes until smooth and elastic.

Rest 2 hours at room temperature, then divide into 4 balls and refrigerate 24-48 hours. This long cold ferment is what gives Neapolitan dough its flavor and its blistered crust - there is no shortcut.
Take the dough out 2 hours before baking. Heat your oven as hot as it goes, 500-550F, with a pizza steel or stone inside for a full hour.
Crush the tomatoes by hand with the salt. Do not cook the sauce; it cooks on the pizza.
Stretch a dough ball by hand on a semolina-dusted surface, pressing from the center outward and leaving a thick rim. Never use a rolling pin - it crushes the gas you spent two days building.
Top with a thin layer of sauce, the drained mozzarella and a drizzle of oil, then bake 6-8 minutes until the crust is puffed and charred in spots. Add the basil as it comes out.

title: Sheet Pan Pizza
description: Thick-crust pan pizza with a fried, crisp bottom. No stone or peel needed.
steps: Stir the flour, warm water, yeast, salt and sugar together into a sticky dough. No kneading needed - just mix until uniform.
Pour 3 tbsp of the oil into a half sheet pan, add the dough, turn it to coat and cover. Let it rise 2 hours until puffy.
Press the dough out to the corners of the pan with oiled fingers. If it springs back, wait 15 minutes and press again.
Heat the oven to 475F. Spread the sauce to within an inch of the edges, then the mozzarella right out to the edge - cheese touching the hot pan is what makes the crisp, caramelized rim.
Add the Parmesan and oregano and drizzle with the remaining oil.
Bake on the lowest rack 20-25 minutes until the bottom is golden and crisp. Slide out of the pan onto a rack immediately so the base does not steam. Add basil.

title: Pepperoni Pizza
description: The American favorite, with cupped pepperoni crisped at the edges.
steps: Put a pizza steel or an upside-down sheet pan in the oven and heat to 525F for a full 45 minutes. A properly preheated surface is the single biggest difference between home and pizzeria pizza.
Let the dough sit at room temperature 30 minutes, then stretch it by hand on a semolina-dusted peel or board.
Spread a thin layer of sauce, then the mozzarella, then the pepperoni. Use the small, thick-cut kind if you can find it - it curls into crisp cups.
Slide the pizza onto the hot surface and bake 8-10 minutes until the crust is browned and the pepperoni edges have crisped.
Finish with Parmesan, oregano, pepper flakes and a drizzle of oil.
Cut on a rack rather than a board so the bottom stays crisp.

title: White Pizza
description: No tomato: ricotta, mozzarella, garlic oil and rosemary.
steps: Heat the oven to 525F with a steel or inverted sheet pan inside for 45 minutes.
Warm the olive oil with the garlic over low heat 3 minutes, just to soften it. Raw minced garlic scorches on a 525F pizza.
Stretch the dough on a semolina-dusted peel and brush all over with the garlic oil.
Scatter the mozzarella, then dollop the ricotta in spoonfuls - spreading it makes the pizza wet.
Add the Parmesan, rosemary, salt and pepper.
Bake 8-10 minutes until puffed and golden with browned cheese. Finish with more oil.

title: Calzone
description: Pizza dough folded over ricotta and salami, baked until puffed and golden.
steps: Heat the oven to 450F. Mix the ricotta, mozzarella, Parmesan, salami, one egg, oregano, salt and pepper. Keep the filling thick - wet filling steams the dough from inside and tears it.
Divide the dough into 4 and stretch each into an oval.
Put filling on half of each oval, leaving a 1-inch border, then fold the dough over and press the edges together. Crimp with a fork or roll the edge into a rope.
Cut two small vents in the top of each. Without vents, the steam has nowhere to go and they burst.
Brush with the beaten egg and olive oil and set on a lined sheet pan.
Bake 20-25 minutes until deep golden and firm. Rest 5 minutes, then serve with warm marinara for dipping.

title: Rosemary Focaccia
description: Dimpled, olive-oil-rich bread with a crisp bottom and open crumb.
steps: Stir the flour, water, yeast, salt and sugar into a very wet, sticky dough. Do not knead and do not add more flour - the high hydration is what creates the open holes.
Cover and let it rise 2 hours until doubled and bubbly.
Pour 1/4 cup of the oil into a 9x13 pan, scrape the dough in and turn it to coat. Rest 20 minutes.
Oil your fingers and press straight down through the dough all over to make deep dimples, stretching it to the corners.
Drizzle the rest of the oil over, pushing it into the dimples, then scatter the rosemary and flaky salt. Rise 30 more minutes.
Bake at 425F for 25-30 minutes until deep golden. Turn it out of the pan onto a rack right away so the bottom stays crisp.

title: Garlic Bread
description: Split loaf loaded with garlic butter and broiled until the edges char.
steps: Mash the softened butter with the garlic, Parmesan, parsley, salt and pepper flakes.
Spread it thickly over both cut halves, right to the edges and into any holes in the crumb.
Bake at 400F for 10 minutes until the butter has melted into the bread.
Switch to the broiler for 2-3 minutes until the surface is browned and bubbling at the edges. Do not walk away - it burns in seconds.
Cut into thick slices and serve immediately.

title: Bruschetta al Pomodoro
description: Grilled bread rubbed with garlic, piled with marinated tomatoes and basil.
steps: Seed the tomatoes before dicing, then toss them with the basil, minced garlic, half the oil, the vinegar, salt and pepper. Let them sit 15 minutes.
Drain off the liquid that collects before topping the bread. This is the step that keeps bruschetta from going soggy in thirty seconds.
Brush the bread slices with the remaining oil and grill or broil 2 minutes per side until charred at the edges but still chewy inside.
While each slice is hot, rub it once with a cut clove of raw garlic. The rough toast acts like a grater.
Spoon the tomatoes on top, add Parmesan and a last drizzle of oil, and serve immediately.

title: Stromboli
description: Dough rolled around cold cuts and cheese, baked into a sliceable log.
steps: Roll the dough into a large rectangle about 1/4 inch thick on parchment.
Layer the meats, then the cheeses and peppers, leaving a 1-inch border all around. Season with the oregano and garlic powder.
Roll it up tightly from one long side, like a jelly roll, using the parchment to help. Pinch the seam and both ends closed firmly.
Set it seam-side down, brush with the egg, scatter the sesame seeds and cut 4 diagonal slashes in the top to vent.
Bake at 400F for 28-32 minutes until deep golden and firm.
Rest 10 minutes before slicing - cut it hot and the cheese runs out. Serve with marinara.

title: No-Knead Pizza Dough
description: Four ingredients, no kneading, an overnight rise in the fridge.
steps: Stir the flour, water, yeast and salt together with a spoon for 60 seconds until there is no dry flour left. It will look rough and shaggy - that is correct.
Cover and leave at room temperature 2 hours, then refrigerate 18-24 hours. Time does the work that kneading otherwise would, and the cold rise builds real flavor.
Turn the dough onto a floured surface, divide into 4 pieces and shape each into a tight ball by dragging it against the counter.
Set the balls on an oiled tray, cover, and let them come to room temperature for 2 hours before stretching. Cold dough will not stretch - it snaps back.
Stretch by hand, never with a rolling pin, and top as you like.
Bake at the highest temperature your oven reaches on a preheated steel or stone, 7-10 minutes.

title: Arancini
description: Risotto balls with a molten mozzarella core, breaded and deep-fried.
ingredients: 8 oz mozzarella, cut in small cubes
steps: Make a firm risotto: cook the onion in the butter, add the rice and toast 2 minutes, add the wine, then the warm broth a ladle at a time with the saffron, stirring, 18 minutes. Stop while it is firmer and drier than you would serve - loose risotto cannot be rolled.
Beat in the Parmesan and salt, spread on a sheet pan and refrigerate at least 4 hours or overnight. Cold rice is the only workable rice.
Scoop a golf ball of rice into your wet palm, press a cube of mozzarella into the center and close the rice completely around it. Any gap will leak cheese into the oil.
Roll each ball in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs. For the sturdiest crust, do egg and breadcrumbs twice.
Heat 3 inches of oil to 350F and fry 3-4 at a time for 4-5 minutes, turning, until deep golden.
Drain on a rack and salt immediately. Rest 5 minutes before biting in - the centers are molten. Serve with marinara.

title: Garlic Knots
description: Pizza dough tied in knots, baked, then tossed in garlic butter and Parmesan.
steps: Divide the dough into 12 pieces and roll each into a 6-inch rope.
Tie each rope in a simple overhand knot and tuck the ends underneath so they do not unravel in the oven.
Set them on a lined sheet pan an inch apart and bake at 425F for 15-18 minutes until golden.
Melt the butter with the garlic over low heat 2 minutes - gently, so the garlic softens without browning.
Toss the hot knots in the garlic butter in a large bowl while they are still straight out of the oven, so they drink it in.
Add the Parmesan, parsley, salt and pepper flakes and toss again. Serve with marinara.

title: Caprese Salad
description: Tomato, mozzarella and basil with oil and salt. Nothing to hide behind.
steps: Take the mozzarella out of the fridge 30 minutes ahead. Cold mozzarella is rubbery and tastes of nothing, and this dish is only as good as its ingredients.
Slice the tomatoes and mozzarella about the same thickness and overlap them on a platter, tucking whole basil leaves between.
Season the tomatoes themselves with the flaky salt - seasoning the surface is not the same thing.
Drizzle generously with olive oil and add the black pepper.
Add the balsamic glaze only if you like it; in Capri it would not appear. Serve within minutes of assembling.

title: Antipasto Platter
description: Cured meats, cheeses, olives and marinated vegetables, arranged not cooked.
steps: Take everything out of the refrigerator 30 minutes before serving. Cold cured meat and cheese taste flat.
Drape the prosciutto in loose folds rather than laying it flat - it should look airy, and it is easier to pick up.
Fan the salami and capicola in overlapping rows and set the cheeses in separate groups across the board.
Put the wet items - artichokes, peppers, olives, pepperoncini - in small bowls so their brine does not run across the meat.
Fill the gaps with cherry tomatoes, drizzle the vegetables with olive oil and sprinkle the oregano.
Serve with sliced bread alongside.

title: Insalata Tricolore
description: Arugula, radicchio and endive in a sharp lemon dressing.
steps: Wash and dry the greens thoroughly. Wet leaves repel dressing, and this salad is all leaves.
Whisk the oil, lemon juice, Dijon, salt and pepper into an emulsified dressing.
Toss the greens with just enough dressing to coat - these are bitter leaves and will go limp if drowned.
Taste and add more lemon or salt. Bitterness needs both acid and salt to read as pleasant rather than harsh.
Top with shaved Parmesan and serve immediately.

title: Panzanella
description: Stale bread salad soaked in tomato juices, oil and vinegar.
ingredients: 1 lb day-old Italian bread, torn in chunks
2 lb ripe tomatoes, cut in chunks
steps: Toast the torn bread on a sheet pan at 375F for 10-12 minutes until dry and lightly golden. It needs to be genuinely dry so it can drink the dressing without collapsing.
Toss the tomato chunks with 1 tsp of the salt and let them sit 15 minutes in a colander over a bowl to collect the juices.
Whisk those collected tomato juices with the oil, vinegar, garlic, remaining salt and pepper. This is the dressing, and it is the whole point.
Combine the bread, tomatoes, cucumber and onion and pour the dressing over.
Let it stand 30 minutes at room temperature, tossing once, so the bread softens unevenly - some chunks soaked, some still chewy.
Fold in the basil just before serving.

title: Prosciutto e Melone
description: Salty cured ham draped over cold sweet melon. Two ingredients.
ingredients: 8 oz thinly sliced prosciutto di Parma
steps: Chill the melon thoroughly, then halve it, scoop out the seeds and cut into thin wedges or thick batons.
Have the prosciutto sliced as thinly as the deli can manage - thick prosciutto is chewy and overwhelming.
Drape a slice loosely over each piece of melon rather than wrapping it tightly.
Drizzle with a little olive oil, add black pepper and scatter the mint.
Serve immediately while the melon is still cold and the ham is at room temperature. That contrast is the dish.

title: Italian Stuffed Mushrooms
description: Mushroom caps filled with garlicky breadcrumbs, Parmesan and herbs.
steps: Pull the stems out of the mushrooms and chop them finely. Wipe the caps with a damp towel rather than rinsing - mushrooms are sponges and wet caps release water into the filling.
Cook the chopped stems in 2 tbsp oil over medium-high 6 minutes until all their liquid has evaporated, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Mix them with the breadcrumbs, 1 cup Parmesan, parsley, cream cheese, oregano, salt and pepper.
Mound the filling into the caps, pressing it in firmly, and set them on a sheet pan.
Drizzle with the remaining oil and scatter the rest of the Parmesan over.
Bake at 400F for 20-25 minutes until the tops are browned and the mushrooms have released a little liquid. Serve warm.

title: Fried Calamari
description: Flour-dusted squid rings fried 90 seconds and served with lemon.
ingredients: 2 lb cleaned squid, bodies sliced in rings
steps: Soak the squid rings in the milk for 15 minutes, then drain well. The milk tenderizes them slightly and helps the flour stick.
Mix the flour, cornstarch, salt, pepper, garlic powder and cayenne. The cornstarch is what makes the coating light and crisp rather than bready.
Heat 3 inches of oil to 375F. Use a thermometer; cooler oil means greasy, chewy calamari.
Toss a handful of drained squid in the flour, shake off the excess in a sieve, and lower it into the oil.
Fry 90 seconds only, until pale gold. Squid goes from tender to rubber in about 30 seconds past that point.
Drain on a rack, salt immediately, and serve with lemon, parsley and marinara. Fry in small batches so the oil stays hot.

title: Beef Carpaccio
description: Raw beef pounded paper-thin with arugula, Parmesan and lemon.
steps: Buy the freshest tenderloin you can from a butcher you trust and tell them it is for carpaccio - this dish is served raw, so sourcing matters more than technique.
Wrap the beef tightly in plastic and freeze 45-60 minutes until firm but not frozen solid. This is what makes thin slicing possible.
Slice as thinly as you can, then lay each slice between sheets of plastic and pound gently with a flat mallet until nearly translucent.
Arrange the slices in a single layer covering each plate.
Whisk the oil, lemon juice, Dijon and capers and spoon it over the beef. Season with flaky salt and pepper.
Pile arugula in the center, add shaved Parmesan and serve immediately with lemon wedges.

title: Caponata
description: Sicilian sweet-and-sour eggplant with capers, olives and vinegar.
steps: Salt the cubed eggplant and leave it in a colander 30 minutes, then rinse and press dry.
Fry the eggplant in batches in most of the oil over medium-high until deep golden, 8 minutes per batch, and drain. Crowding the pan steams it into grey mush.
Cook the onion and celery in the remaining oil 8 minutes, then the garlic for 1.
Add the tomatoes, vinegar and sugar and simmer 15 minutes. The balance of sweet and sour is the defining feature, so taste and adjust both.
Return the eggplant and add the olives, capers and raisins. Simmer 10 minutes until thick and jammy.
Cool to room temperature, then fold in the pine nuts and basil. Caponata tastes markedly better the next day.

title: Burrata with Tomatoes
description: A torn ball of burrata spilling cream over marinated tomatoes and basil.
steps: Take the burrata out of the refrigerator 20 minutes before serving. Cold burrata will not spill properly and tastes of very little.
Toss the tomatoes with the oil, vinegar, garlic, half the basil, 1 tsp salt and the pepper. Let them marinate 10 minutes.
Spoon the tomatoes and their juices onto a shallow platter.
Set the burrata in the middle and tear it open with your fingers or a knife tip so the cream runs into the tomatoes.
Finish with the rest of the basil, flaky salt, pepper and a last drizzle of oil. Serve with grilled bread.

title: Risotto alla Milanese
description: Saffron risotto, stirred patiently, finished with butter and Parmesan.
steps: Keep the broth at a bare simmer in a separate pot and steep the saffron in a ladleful of it. Cold broth added to risotto stops the cooking and makes it gluey.
Cook the onion in 3 tbsp butter over medium 6 minutes until soft but not browned.
Add the rice and toast 2 minutes, stirring, until the grains look translucent at the edges with a white center.
Add the wine and stir until it has been absorbed.

Add the hot broth one ladle at a time, stirring often and waiting until each addition is nearly absorbed before adding the next. This takes 18-20 minutes - the stirring is what releases the starch that makes it creamy.
Off the heat, beat in the remaining butter and the Parmesan vigorously. Season and serve immediately; risotto waits for no one and should ripple when you shake the plate.

title: Mushroom Risotto
description: Earthy risotto with browned mushrooms and dried porcini broth.
steps: Soak the dried porcini in a cup of hot broth 20 minutes, then chop them and strain the soaking liquid into the rest of the broth. That liquid carries most of the mushroom flavor, so do not discard it.
Brown the fresh mushrooms in the olive oil over high heat, undisturbed for 4 minutes before stirring, until deeply colored. Salt them only at the end or they will steam.
Cook the onion in 3 tbsp butter 6 minutes, add the garlic for 1, then the rice, toasting 2 minutes.
Add the wine and stir until absorbed, then begin adding the hot broth a ladle at a time, stirring, for 18-20 minutes.
Stir in the chopped porcini and most of the browned mushrooms in the last 5 minutes.
Off the heat, beat in the remaining butter and the Parmesan. Season and top with the reserved mushrooms and parsley.

title: Lemon Risotto
description: Bright, creamy risotto finished with lemon zest, juice and mascarpone.
steps: Keep the broth hot in a separate pan throughout.
Cook the shallot in 2 tbsp butter over medium 4 minutes, then add the rice and toast 2 minutes.
Add the wine, stir until absorbed, then add the hot broth a ladle at a time with the lemon zest, stirring, for 18-20 minutes until the rice is al dente with a creamy sauce around it.
Take the pan off the heat before adding the lemon juice - acid in a hot pan can make the rice seize and the dairy split.
Beat in the remaining butter, the mascarpone and the Parmesan.
Season well and finish with basil. Serve at once in warm bowls.

title: Creamy Polenta with Mushrooms
description: Soft cornmeal with butter and Parmesan under garlicky browned mushrooms.
steps: Bring the water to a boil with the salt and pour the polenta in a slow stream while whisking constantly. Adding it all at once guarantees lumps.
Lower the heat to the barest simmer and cook 35-40 minutes, stirring every few minutes and scraping the bottom. Coarse polenta cannot be hurried; instant polenta is a different and lesser dish.
Beat in the butter and Parmesan off the heat. It should be pourable, not stiff - loosen with hot water if needed.
Meanwhile brown the mushrooms in the olive oil over high heat, undisturbed 4 minutes, then stir and cook 4 more.
Add the garlic and thyme for 1 minute, then the wine, and reduce 2 minutes, scraping the pan.
Spoon the polenta into shallow bowls, top with the mushrooms and their juices, and finish with pepper and parsley.

title: Minestrone
description: A big vegetable soup with beans and pasta, built from whatever is in season.
ingredients: 2 cans (15 oz each) cannellini beans, drained
steps: Cook the onion, carrots and celery in the oil over medium 10 minutes until soft - this slow start is what gives the soup its sweetness.
Add the garlic and tomato paste and cook 2 minutes.
Add the zucchini and cabbage for 4 minutes, then the tomatoes, beans, broth, Parmesan rind, dried herbs, salt and pepper.
Simmer 25 minutes, then add the pasta and green beans and cook until the pasta is al dente, 9 minutes.
Fish out the Parmesan rind. If making ahead, cook the pasta separately - it swells and goes mushy overnight in the pot.
Serve with Parmesan, fresh basil and a heavy drizzle of olive oil.

title: Ribollita
description: Tuscan bread and bean soup, thick enough to eat with a fork.
ingredients: 2 cans (15 oz each) cannellini beans, drained
steps: Render the pancetta in the oil, then add the onion, carrots and celery and cook 10 minutes.
Add the garlic and tomato paste for 2 minutes, then the kale and cook until wilted, 4 minutes.
Mash one can of the beans and add them along with the whole beans, tomatoes, broth, Parmesan rind, rosemary, pepper flakes and salt.
Simmer 30 minutes, then remove the rind and rosemary stems.
Stir in the torn stale bread and simmer 10 more minutes until it has completely broken down and the soup is very thick. Ribollita means reboiled, and it is meant to be a porridge rather than a broth.
Let it sit 10 minutes, then serve with Parmesan and a generous pour of olive oil.

title: Chicken Parmesan
description: Breaded cutlets under marinara and mozzarella, broiled until blistered.
ingredients: 4 boneless chicken breasts, halved and pounded thin
steps: Pound the cutlets to an even 1/2 inch. Even thickness is what lets them cook through before the crust burns.
Mix the breadcrumbs with half the Parmesan, the salt, pepper and garlic powder. Set up flour, egg and breadcrumb dishes.
Coat each cutlet in flour, egg, then breadcrumbs, pressing firmly. Rest on a rack 10 minutes so the coating sets.
Fry in 1/2 inch of oil over medium-high, 3 minutes per side, until deep golden. Drain on a rack.
Set the cutlets in a baking dish, spoon marinara over the center of each but leave the edges of the crust exposed so they stay crisp, then top with mozzarella and the rest of the Parmesan.
Bake at 425F for 10 minutes, then broil 2-3 minutes until the cheese blisters. Finish with basil.

title: Chicken Marsala
description: Pan-fried cutlets in a mushroom and Marsala wine sauce.
steps: Pound the cutlets thin, season, and dredge in the flour, shaking off the excess. That thin flour coat both browns and thickens the sauce later.
Sear them in the oil and 2 tbsp butter over medium-high, 3-4 minutes per side, then move to a plate.
Brown the mushrooms in the same pan over high heat 6 minutes without stirring much, then add the shallots for 3 minutes and the garlic for 1.
Pour in the Marsala and let it reduce by half, 4 minutes, scraping up the browned bits. Use dry Marsala, not sweet, unless you want a dessert sauce.
Add the broth and reduce 5 minutes, then the cream, and simmer 3 minutes until it coats a spoon.
Return the chicken with any resting juices for 2 minutes, swirl in the last butter off the heat, and finish with parsley.

title: Chicken Piccata
description: Cutlets in a lemon, caper and butter sauce. Twenty-five minutes.
steps: Pound the cutlets to 1/2 inch, season and dredge in flour, shaking off the excess.
Sear in the oil and 2 tbsp butter over medium-high 3 minutes per side until golden, then move to a plate.
Add the garlic to the pan for 30 seconds, then the wine, and reduce by half while scraping up the browned bits.
Add the broth and lemon slices and reduce 4 minutes.
Take the pan off the heat and whisk in the remaining butter a piece at a time. Off-heat is what emulsifies the sauce instead of splitting it into a greasy puddle.
Stir in the lemon juice and capers, return the chicken for 1 minute, and finish with parsley.

title: Chicken Cacciatore
description: Hunter's chicken braised with peppers, tomatoes, olives and wine.
steps: Pat the chicken very dry, season well, and brown it skin-side down in the oil for 7 minutes, then 3 on the second side. Dry skin and a hot pan are what give you color here.
Move the chicken out and pour off most of the fat.
Cook the onion, peppers and mushrooms 8 minutes, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the wine and reduce by half, scraping the pan, then the tomatoes, olives, oregano, pepper flakes and bay leaves.
Nestle the chicken back in skin-side up, leaving the skin above the liquid so it does not go soggy. Simmer uncovered 40 minutes.
Discard the bay leaves, taste for salt and finish with basil. Serve with polenta or bread.

title: Chicken Saltimbocca
description: Cutlets wrapped in prosciutto and sage, seared and finished with wine butter.
steps: Pound the cutlets thin and season lightly - the prosciutto is already salty.
Lay 2 sage leaves on each cutlet, then wrap a slice of prosciutto around to hold them, pressing it on firmly so it adheres.
Dredge only the exposed chicken side in flour, not the prosciutto.
Sear prosciutto-side down first in the oil and 1 tbsp butter over medium-high for 3 minutes, pressing with a spatula so it crisps, then flip for 3 minutes.
Move the chicken out. Add the wine and reduce by half, then the broth, and reduce 3 minutes.
Off the heat, whisk in the remaining butter and the lemon juice, then spoon the sauce over the cutlets.

title: Eggplant Parmesan
description: Fried eggplant layered with marinara and cheese and baked.
steps: Salt the eggplant slices and lay them in a colander for 45 minutes, then press them dry between towels. This removes bitterness and, more importantly, water that would make the finished dish soupy.
Mix the breadcrumbs with half the Parmesan and the pepper. Coat each slice in flour, egg, then breadcrumbs.
Fry in 1/2 inch of oil over medium-high, 2-3 minutes per side, until golden. Drain on racks, not paper towels, so they stay crisp.
Spread a thin layer of marinara in a 9x13 dish, then layer eggplant, sauce, mozzarella, Parmesan and basil. Repeat three times.
Keep the sauce sparing between layers - this is the difference between sliceable and sloppy.
Bake at 375F for 40-45 minutes until bubbling and browned. Rest 20 minutes before cutting.

title: Osso Buco
description: Veal shanks braised three hours with wine and gremolata to finish.
ingredients: 3 cloves garlic, minced, for the gremolata
steps: Tie a length of kitchen twine around the circumference of each shank. Without it the meat falls off the bone during the braise and loses its shape on the plate.
Season and dredge the shanks in flour, then brown them hard in the oil on both sides, 5 minutes per side. Do this in batches.
Cook the onion, carrots and celery in the same pot 10 minutes, then the garlic for 1 and the tomato paste for 2.
Add the wine and reduce by half, scraping the bottom, then the broth, bay leaves and thyme.
Return the shanks standing upright so the marrow stays in the bone, cover and braise at 325F for 2.5-3 hours until a fork slides into the meat with no resistance.
Mix the lemon zest, parsley and raw garlic into a gremolata and scatter it over just before serving. That raw, sharp finish is what cuts three hours of richness.

title: Beef Braciole
description: Thin beef rolled around breadcrumbs, cheese and herbs, braised in sauce.
ingredients: 2 lb beef top round, sliced thin and pounded
steps: Pound the beef slices between plastic to about 1/4 inch - thin and even, or they will not roll without tearing.
Mix the breadcrumbs, Pecorino, half the garlic, the parsley, pine nuts, raisins, salt, pepper and 2 tbsp oil into a filling.

Spread a thin layer of filling on each slice, leaving a border, then roll up tightly from the short end and tie with twine in two places. Overfilling is the most common mistake - it bursts out during the braise.
Brown the rolls in the remaining oil on all sides, 6 minutes, then set aside.
Cook the onion 6 minutes, add the rest of the garlic, then the wine, reducing by half. Add the tomatoes and oregano.
Return the rolls, cover and simmer very gently 2-2.5 hours until the beef is fork-tender. Rest 10 minutes, snip the twine and slice into pinwheels. Serve the sauce over rigatoni.

title: Porchetta
description: Herb-stuffed pork belly rolled around loin and roasted to crackling.
ingredients: 1 skin-on pork belly (5 lb), with a 3 lb pork loin
steps: Toast the fennel seeds and peppercorns in a dry pan 1 minute, then crush them coarsely. Mix with the garlic, rosemary, sage, lemon zest, half the salt and the pepper flakes.
Lay the belly skin-side down and score the meat in a crosshatch. Rub the herb mixture over the meat side only - never on the skin, which must stay dry.
Set the loin along one edge and roll the belly tightly around it, then tie with twine every 1 1/2 inches.
Score the skin in fine lines, rub it with the remaining salt and refrigerate uncovered at least 24 hours. This drying step is the only way to get real crackling.
Roast at 275F for 3 hours until the center reads 145F, then raise the heat to 500F for 20-30 minutes, turning as needed, until the skin blisters and crackles all over. Watch it closely at this stage.
Rest 20 minutes, then cut through the crackling with a serrated knife into thick slices.

title: Sausage and Peppers
description: Italian sausages roasted on one pan with peppers and onions.
steps: Heat the oven to 425F. Toss the peppers, onions and garlic with the oil, oregano, pepper flakes, salt and pepper on a large sheet pan.
Nestle the whole sausages among the vegetables. Do not prick them - the casings keep the juices in.
Roast 20 minutes, then turn the sausages and stir the vegetables.
Roast 15-20 minutes more until the sausages are browned and read 160F and the peppers are soft with charred edges.
Toss everything with the vinegar right out of the oven. The acid cuts the fat and wakes the whole pan up.
Serve in hoagie rolls or over polenta.

title: Meatballs al Forno
description: Baked meatballs finished in marinara under melted mozzarella.
steps: Soak the breadcrumbs in the milk 5 minutes. This panade is what keeps baked meatballs from turning into dense pucks.
Mix in both meats, the eggs, 1 cup Parmesan, the garlic, parsley, salt, pepper and pepper flakes with your hands, stopping the moment it comes together.
Roll into 24 balls and set them on a lined sheet pan with space between.
Bake at 425F for 18 minutes until browned.
Pour the marinara into a baking dish, add the meatballs, scatter the mozzarella and remaining Parmesan over.
Bake 15 minutes more until bubbling and the cheese has browned in spots. Finish with basil.

title: Chicken Francese
description: Egg-battered cutlets in a lemon butter wine sauce. Lighter than piccata.
steps: Beat the eggs with the Parmesan and a pinch of salt. Season and pound the cutlets thin.

Dredge each cutlet in flour, then dip it in the egg mixture, letting the excess drip off. Flour first, egg second - this order is what makes Francese different from piccata, and it gives a soft, almost souffled coating.
Fry in the oil and 2 tbsp butter over medium heat, 3 minutes per side, until pale golden. Keep the heat moderate so the egg does not brown too fast.
Move the chicken out and wipe the pan if there are burnt bits.
Add the wine and reduce by half, then the broth and lemon slices, and reduce 4 minutes.
Off the heat, whisk in the remaining butter and the lemon juice, return the chicken briefly, and finish with parsley.

title: Branzino al Forno
description: Whole sea bass roasted with lemon, herbs and olive oil.
ingredients: 2 whole branzino (1 1/2 lb each), cleaned and scaled
steps: Heat the oven to 425F. Pat the fish completely dry inside and out and score the skin three times on each side.
Season the cavities well and stuff them with lemon slices, thyme, parsley and garlic.
Set the fish in an oiled roasting pan, scatter the tomatoes around, pour the wine into the pan and drizzle everything with oil. Season the skin with flaky salt.
Roast 25-30 minutes. The fish is done when the flesh at the thickest part near the head is opaque and pulls cleanly from the bone - about 130F.
Rest 5 minutes. To serve, run a knife along the spine and lift the top fillet off, then lift the backbone away to free the bottom fillet.
Spoon the pan juices and burst tomatoes over each portion.

title: Shrimp Fra Diavolo
description: Shrimp in a fiery garlic-chile tomato sauce over linguine.
steps: Pat the shrimp dry and sear them in 2 tbsp of the oil over high heat, 1 minute per side, then pull them out. They will finish in the sauce, so undercook them here.
Lower the heat, add the remaining oil, the garlic, pepper flakes and cayenne and cook 1 minute. The dish is called brother devil for a reason - the heat should be assertive.
Add the wine and reduce by half, scraping the pan.
Add the tomatoes, salt and oregano and simmer 15 minutes until thickened.
Boil the linguine to al dente, then add it to the sauce with a splash of pasta water.
Return the shrimp for 1-2 minutes only, swirl in the butter off the heat and finish with parsley. No cheese.

title: Cioppino
description: San Francisco's Italian fisherman's stew, loaded with shellfish and fish.
ingredients: 1 lb firm white fish, cut in chunks
steps: Cook the fennel and onion in the oil 10 minutes until soft, then add the garlic, pepper flakes and tomato paste for 2 minutes.
Add the wine and reduce by a third, then the tomatoes, broth, bay leaves, oregano and salt. Simmer 25 minutes. The broth can be made entirely ahead; only the seafood is last-minute.
Add the clams, cover and cook 4 minutes.
Add the mussels and cook 3 minutes until they open.
Add the fish, shrimp and scallops, cover and cook 3-4 minutes until the fish just flakes. Everything goes in by cooking time, longest first - this staggering is the whole technique.
Discard any unopened shells and the bay leaves, add the parsley, and serve in wide bowls with crusty bread.

title: Italian Wedding Soup
description: Tiny meatballs and acini di pepe in a clear broth with escarole.
ingredients: 1 lb ground beef and pork mix
steps: Soak the breadcrumbs in the milk 5 minutes, then mix with the meat, egg, half the Parmesan, the garlic, parsley, 1 tsp salt and the pepper.
Roll into very small meatballs, about 3/4 inch - marble-sized is traditional and they cook through in the broth.
Cook the onion, carrots and celery in the oil 8 minutes, then add the broth and bring to a gentle simmer.
Drop the meatballs in and simmer 10 minutes without stirring hard, so they hold together.
Add the pasta and cook 8 minutes, then the escarole for 3 minutes until wilted.
Season with the remaining salt and the nutmeg and serve with the rest of the Parmesan.

title: Chicken Milanese
description: A thin breaded cutlet fried crisp, topped with dressed arugula.
ingredients: 4 boneless chicken breasts, halved and pounded very thin
steps: Pound the cutlets to 1/4 inch, as thin as you can without tearing. The thinness is the dish - it should cover the plate.
Mix the breadcrumbs with the Parmesan, salt and pepper. Coat each cutlet in flour, egg, then breadcrumbs, pressing firmly.
Fry in 1/4 inch of oil over medium-high, 2-3 minutes per side, until deep golden. Work one or two at a time so the oil stays hot.
Drain on a rack and salt immediately.
Toss the arugula and tomatoes with the olive oil, lemon juice and a pinch of salt.
Pile the salad on top of each hot cutlet and serve with lemon wedges.

title: Pork Chops with Vinegar Peppers
description: Seared chops finished with pickled peppers and a sharp pan sauce.
ingredients: 2 cups pickled hot peppers, sliced, plus 1/3 cup of their brine
steps: Pat the chops very dry and season well. Sear them in the oil over high heat 4 minutes per side until deeply browned, then move to a plate. They should not be cooked through yet.
Lower the heat and cook the onion 6 minutes, then add the garlic and rosemary for 1 minute.
Add the pickled peppers and their brine and let it bubble 2 minutes, scraping the pan.
Add the broth and return the chops with any juices. Simmer 8-10 minutes, turning once, until they read 145F.
Move the chops to a board to rest and whisk the butter into the pan sauce off the heat.
Taste the sauce - it should be sharp and hot, not mellow. Spoon it over the chops with parsley.

title: Salsiccia e Fagioli
description: Italian sausage braised with white beans, tomato and greens.
ingredients: 3 cans (15 oz each) cannellini beans, drained
steps: Brown the whole sausages in the oil over medium-high, turning, 8 minutes. Take them out and slice into thick coins.
Cook the onion in the same pot 6 minutes, then add the garlic, pepper flakes and tomato paste for 2 minutes.
Mash a cup of the beans and add them with the rest of the beans, the broth and the rosemary. The mashed beans thicken the braise naturally.
Return the sausage and simmer 15 minutes.
Stir in the kale and cook 5 minutes until tender. Season.
Pull out the rosemary stems and serve in bowls with Parmesan, olive oil and crusty bread.

title: Meatball Sub
description: Meatballs and marinara in a toasted roll under broiled mozzarella.
steps: Warm the meatballs in the marinara over low heat 10 minutes so they absorb the sauce.
Mash the butter with the garlic, spread it on the cut rolls and toast them at 400F for 5 minutes. Toasting the bread first is what stops the sauce soaking straight through.
Set 4 meatballs in each roll and spoon sauce over, but not so much that it pools.
Cover with mozzarella and Parmesan and sprinkle the oregano over.
Broil 3-4 minutes until the cheese is melted and browned in spots.
Finish with basil and serve immediately.

title: Italian Sub
description: Layered cold cuts, provolone, lettuce and an oregano vinaigrette.
steps: Whisk the oil, vinegar, oregano, salt and pepper into a vinaigrette.
Hollow out a little of the soft interior of each roll so the fillings sit down in the bread rather than sliding off.
Layer the cheese first, directly on the bottom bread. It acts as a barrier against the dressing.
Add the meats in loose folds rather than flat stacks, then the lettuce, tomato, onion and pepperoncini.
Spoon the vinaigrette over the lettuce, not the bread.
Press the sandwich closed firmly, wrap it tightly in paper for 10 minutes if you can wait, then cut on a diagonal.

title: Chicken Parm Sandwich
description: A breaded cutlet, marinara and melted mozzarella in a crusty roll.
steps: Pound the cutlets to an even 1/2 inch and season. Mix the breadcrumbs with half the Parmesan.
Coat each cutlet in flour, egg, then breadcrumbs, pressing firmly, and rest 10 minutes.
Fry in 1/2 inch of oil over medium-high 3 minutes per side until deep golden, then drain on a rack.
Toast the split rolls under the broiler 2 minutes.
Set a cutlet in each roll, spoon marinara over the middle of the cutlet and pile on the mozzarella and remaining Parmesan.
Broil the open sandwiches 3 minutes until the cheese bubbles, then add basil and close. Keeping sauce off the bread is what keeps it from going limp.

title: Muffuletta
description: New Orleans Sicilian sandwich with olive salad, pressed for hours.
ingredients: 1 round sesame muffuletta loaf or focaccia
steps: Mix both olives, the artichokes, giardiniera, garlic, oregano, oil and vinegar into the olive salad. Let it sit at least 30 minutes - overnight is better.
Split the loaf horizontally and scoop out a little of the soft interior from both halves.
Spoon olive salad with its oil onto both cut surfaces, pressing it in. The oil soaking into the bread is the entire character of this sandwich.
Layer the meats and cheeses on the bottom half, alternating, then add more olive salad and close it.
Wrap the whole thing tightly in plastic, set a heavy pan or a few cans on top and press 2 hours at room temperature or up to overnight in the fridge.
Cut into wedges. It is meant to be eaten at room temperature, not hot.

title: Tiramisu
description: Espresso-soaked savoiardi layered with mascarpone cream and cocoa.
steps: Whisk the yolks and sugar in a bowl set over barely simmering water for 8-10 minutes until thick, pale and hot to the touch. This cooks the eggs to a safe temperature and is worth doing properly.
Cool the mixture to room temperature, then beat in the mascarpone until smooth. Cold mascarpone will go lumpy, so take it out of the fridge an hour ahead.
Whip the cream to soft peaks and fold it into the mascarpone in two additions.
Stir the rum into the cooled espresso. Dip each ladyfinger for one second per side only - they are dry biscuits and turn to sludge if they soak.
Line a 9x13 dish with dipped ladyfingers, spread half the cream over, then repeat for a second layer.
Cover and refrigerate at least 6 hours, ideally overnight. Dust heavily with cocoa and shave chocolate over just before serving.

title: Panna Cotta
description: Set cream with vanilla, barely holding its shape. Four ingredients.
ingredients: 1 vanilla bean, split, or 2 tsp vanilla extract
steps: Sprinkle the gelatin over the cold water in a small bowl and leave it 5 minutes to bloom into a solid sponge. Adding dry gelatin to hot cream leaves rubbery threads.
Warm the cream, milk, sugar, salt and the scraped vanilla bean over medium heat until steaming, about 5 minutes. Do not let it boil.
Take it off the heat and whisk in the bloomed gelatin until completely dissolved.
Strain into a jug and pour into 6 ramekins or glasses.
Chill at least 4 hours. The texture should wobble like set custard, not bounce - that is the mark of correctly dosed gelatin.
Serve with berries, either in the glasses or unmolded by dipping each ramekin briefly in hot water.

title: Cannoli
description: Blistered fried shells filled with sweet ricotta at the last moment.
steps: Drain the ricotta in a cheesecloth-lined sieve in the fridge overnight, weighted with a plate. Wet ricotta makes a soupy filling that destroys the shells.
Cut the cold butter into the flour, sugar, salt and cinnamon, then add the egg and Marsala to form a stiff dough. Knead 5 minutes, wrap and rest 1 hour.
Roll the dough paper-thin - you should see the counter through it - and cut 4-inch circles. Wrap each around an oiled cannoli form and seal the overlap with egg white.
Fry two or three at a time in 350F oil for 2-3 minutes until blistered and deep golden. Let them cool before carefully twisting the forms out.
Beat the drained ricotta with the powdered sugar and vanilla until smooth, then fold in the chocolate chips.
Pipe the filling into the shells from both ends only when you are ready to serve. Filled shells go soft within the hour. Dip the ends in pistachios and dust with powdered sugar.

title: Affogato
description: A shot of hot espresso poured over cold vanilla gelato. Done in a minute.
ingredients: 4 scoops vanilla gelato or ice cream
steps: Chill two small glasses in the freezer for a few minutes.
Put two scoops of gelato in each glass.
Pull the espresso and pour it over the gelato immediately, while it is still properly hot. The contrast between hot and frozen is the entire dish, so do not let the coffee sit.
Add the amaretto if using, shave chocolate over the top and serve with a spoon right away.

title: Lemon Granita
description: Sicilian ice scraped into crystals with a fork. No machine needed.
steps: Heat the sugar with 1 cup of the water, stirring until dissolved, then cool completely.
Stir in the remaining water, the lemon juice, zest and salt. Taste it - it should be slightly sweeter and more intense than you want, since freezing mutes flavor.
Pour into a wide shallow metal pan and freeze 45 minutes.
Scrape the whole surface vigorously with a fork, breaking up all the ice crystals.
Repeat the scraping every 30-40 minutes for about 3 hours. The repeated scraping is what makes granita granular rather than a solid block.
Serve in chilled glasses with mint.

title: Almond Biscotti
description: Twice-baked almond cookies, dry and hard, made for dunking.
steps: Heat the oven to 350F. Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder and salt, then stir in the eggs, both extracts, the almonds and lemon zest. The dough will be stiff and sticky.
Divide in two and shape each half into a flat log about 12 inches long and 2 inches wide on a lined sheet pan. Wet your hands to stop it sticking.
Brush with the beaten egg and bake 25-30 minutes until firm and lightly golden.
Cool 15 minutes - long enough to handle but still warm. Cutting them cold shatters them; cutting them hot squashes them.
Slice each log on a diagonal into 1/2-inch pieces with a serrated knife.
Lay the slices cut-side down and bake 10-12 minutes per side until completely dry. They crisp further as they cool and keep for a month in a tin.

title: Zeppole
description: Fried dough puffs tumbled in powdered sugar, eaten hot.
steps: Stir the yeast and sugar into the warm water and wait 10 minutes until foamy. No foam means dead yeast.
Mix in the flour, salt and lemon zest into a very sticky, loose batter - it should be closer to a thick paste than a dough. Do not add extra flour.
Cover and rise 1 hour until doubled and bubbly.
Heat 3 inches of oil to 360F.
Drop heaped tablespoons of batter into the oil using two wet spoons. They will puff and turn themselves over as they cook.
Fry 3-4 minutes until deep golden all over, drain briefly on a rack, then toss in powdered sugar while still hot. Eat within minutes - zeppole do not keep.

title: Italian Ricotta Cheesecake
description: Lighter and drier than New York style, scented with citrus zest.
steps: Drain the ricotta in a cheesecloth-lined sieve overnight in the fridge. Excess whey is what makes a weeping, grainy cheesecake.
Heat the oven to 325F and butter a 9-inch springform pan generously. This cake has no crust, so the pan must be well greased.
Beat the drained ricotta with the sugar for 3 minutes until as smooth as it will get.
Add the eggs one at a time on low speed, then the flour, both zests, vanilla and salt. Mix only until combined - beaten-in air causes cracks.
Pour into the pan and bake 70-80 minutes until the edges are set and the center still wobbles slightly.
Turn the oven off and leave the cake inside with the door ajar for 1 hour, then chill 4 hours. Dust with powdered sugar to serve.

title: Olive Oil Cake
description: A moist, citrus-scented one-bowl cake made with good olive oil.
steps: Heat the oven to 350F and line a 9-inch round pan.
Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda and salt together.
In another bowl whisk the eggs, olive oil, milk, orange zest, juice and vanilla. Use an olive oil you would happily eat on bread - its flavor is the point of the cake.
Pour the wet into the dry and whisk just until smooth.
Bake 45-50 minutes until a skewer comes out clean and the top is deeply golden and cracked.
Cool in the pan 15 minutes, then turn out. It keeps better than butter cakes and is best on day two. Dust with powdered sugar.

title: Panettone
description: Tall, airy Christmas bread with candied fruit. A three-day project.
steps: Soak the raisins and candied peel in the rum for several hours, then drain.
Make a sponge with the yeast, warm milk and 1 cup of the flour and leave it 1 hour until bubbly.

Add the remaining flour, sugar, yolks, eggs, vanilla, zests and salt, then knead 15 minutes. Add the very soft butter a tablespoon at a time, kneading until each is absorbed. This takes another 15 minutes and the dough will look broken before it comes together - keep going.
Rise 3-4 hours until tripled, then fold in the fruit, shape into a ball and drop it into a paper panettone mold. Rise again 4-6 hours until the dough reaches the rim.
Cut a cross in the top, add a knob of butter, and bake at 350F for 50-60 minutes until the center reads 190F. Tent with foil if it darkens early.

Immediately skewer the loaf through the base with two long skewers and hang it upside down until completely cool, at least 4 hours. This sounds absurd and is the only thing that stops the airy crumb collapsing under its own weight.

title: Pizzelle
description: Thin anise waffle cookies pressed in an iron, crisp enough to snap.
steps: Whisk the eggs and sugar until pale, then stir in the melted butter and both extracts.
Fold in the flour, baking powder and salt into a thick batter. Rest it 10 minutes.
Heat the pizzelle iron thoroughly. Test with one cookie first - the first is almost always a throwaway that tells you the right amount of batter and timing.
Drop a rounded teaspoon onto the center of each pattern and close the iron. Press firmly but do not force it.
Cook 45-60 seconds until pale gold. Lift them off with a thin spatula.
Lay each one flat on a rack to cool, or drape it over a rolling pin for curved cookies. They harden within a minute and keep for weeks in a tin.

title: Zabaglione
description: Egg yolks, sugar and Marsala whisked over heat into warm foam.
steps: Set a wide metal bowl over a pan of barely simmering water - the water must not touch the bowl, and it must not boil.
Whisk the yolks, sugar and salt in the bowl until combined, then add the Marsala.
Whisk constantly and vigorously for 8-12 minutes. It will triple in volume and go from thin and yellow to thick, pale and glossy.
It is ready when it holds a ribbon on the surface for a second and reads about 160F. Stop whisking at any point and the eggs will scramble on the bottom of the bowl.
Spoon it warm over berries in glasses and dust with powdered sugar. Zabaglione deflates within minutes, so serve it immediately.

title: Torta Caprese
description: Flourless almond and dark chocolate cake, dense and naturally gluten-free.
steps: Heat the oven to 350F and line a 9-inch springform pan. Melt the chocolate and butter together over low heat, then cool 10 minutes.
Beat the egg yolks with 3/4 cup of the sugar until pale and thick, then fold in the chocolate mixture, almond flour, salt, vanilla and rum.
Beat the egg whites to soft peaks, add the remaining sugar and beat to firm, glossy peaks.
Fold the whites into the batter in three additions, cutting down through the middle and folding over. With no flour, the whites are the only thing lifting this cake - deflate them and it bakes flat.
Bake 40-45 minutes until the top has cracked and a skewer comes out with a few moist crumbs.
Cool completely in the pan. It sinks slightly in the middle, which is correct. Dust heavily with powdered sugar.

title: Aperol Spritz
description: Three parts prosecco, two Aperol, one soda. The Venetian aperitivo.
steps: Fill two large wine glasses completely with ice. A full glass of ice melts more slowly than a few cubes and keeps the drink from going flat and warm.
Pour the prosecco in first, then the Aperol. Adding the prosecco first keeps the bubbles rather than knocking them out.
Top with the soda water.
Stir once, gently, with a bar spoon.
Add an orange slice to each and serve immediately.
